question: If the reporting-alpha split is chosen after seeing the same reliability history, what selection correction preserves simultaneous coverage of the selected pair of V3 bounds?

construction.prior_rule: Precommit allocation-pair masses pi_k summing to 1. For candidate split (a_eq,k, a_exp,k), use channel alphas pi_k*a_eq,k and pi_k*a_exp,k. Then the sum of all 2K marginal error budgets is <= .05; by a union bound all candidate pairs cover simultaneously with probability >= .95, so any post-data selection among those pairs preserves simultaneous coverage.
construction.relation_to_e_BY: Xu, Wang and Ramdas, Post-selection inference for e-value based confidence intervals, arXiv:2203.12572 / EJS 2024, gives FCR control for selected e-CIs under arbitrary selection/dependence. FCR is not the same target as simultaneous coverage of both bounds in the selected allocation pair, so e-BY is not used as a free substitute for this stronger pairwise simultaneous guarantee.

interpretation: Same-history post-selection can be made valid by paying explicit selection complexity, but the finite-horizon cost is large in this tested family.
A precommitted nonuniform allocation prior recovers part of the cost while remaining valid, but still trails a single independently chosen fixed split.
Independent meta-data selection is therefore not merely convenient: when available it can avoid the substantial multiplicity penalty required for arbitrary same-history allocation selection.
scope_guards: Finite nine-allocation grid; no continuum-selection guarantee.
Synthetic stopping times are not production performance.
The post-selection construction guarantees simultaneous coverage by union-bounding all candidate pairs; it is intentionally stronger and generally more conservative than FCR control.
Do not claim e-BY FCR control is equivalent to familywise/simultaneous coverage of the selected two-bound report.

public_source.title: Post-selection inference for e-value based confidence intervals
public_source.authors: Ziyu Xu; Ruodu Wang; Aaditya Ramdas
